findings.reason: a §4 worker dispatched on the followup's "waits on a-project-reads-as-one-picture §2 and §4" would not know §2 here must be merged first, and a `why` view without a table row breaks §2's own gate.
findings.text: §4 says it answers "within its row of the §2 table" and its done-when says the result comes back "all inside its contract", i.e. that row, but §4's declared `depends-on` names only `a-project-reads-as-one-picture#s2` and `#s4`; §2 introduces the table and its test holds "every view of every reckon MCP tool" to its row, so a §4 view landed before §2 has no row and fails.

findings.reason: without the edge a §7 worker is told to start immediately and may put `since` on the snapshot reads only, leaving the brief's change-set unbuilt and the dispatch order wrong, deliberately, for a section that waits on another plan.
findings.text: §7's mechanism extends "the brief" with `since`, and §6 states that brief is the one `a-project-reads-as-one-picture` §7 composes, yet §7 appears in no `plan-section-depends-on` entry while §6 declares the `a-project-reads-as-one-picture` edge for the same artifact; the followup reinforces the error by listing §7 among the sections that "can start at once".

findings.reason: the plan is elsewhere careful to name the signature of a base-arm failure (§3 names the `section_blocking` case, §4 names the unknown-view refusal); here the control needs the same, e.g. that `roadmap view=detail` against `power_convertor` returns `response_over_budget` at base, which §1's own evidence already shows, or the node's whole measure rests on an arm that only proves the table is absent.
findings.text: §2's negative control is the clause "On the base commit at least `roadmap` `view=detail` fails it", but the assertion is "each answer is within its row of the table" and §2 introduces that table in `reckon/mcp_budget.py`, so on the base commit the test cannot fail for the stated reason (a missing row or table errors before any size comparison runs), and the control cannot show the size assertion is falsifiable.

findings.reason: §7's "surface" claim is that no cursor, store or refusal is added, and its done-when ("returns exactly the one section whose declaration moved") cannot be evaluated without a named, timestamped source of section transitions; an unnamed one either does not exist, making the section unbuildable as written, or is a new deliverable the plan has not sized.
findings.text: §7 asserts a change set over "sections whose declaration or readiness moved" and answers "a `since` older than the retained history" in full, but names no store holding a section's declaration transition or that history its retention bound refers to; the only evidence it cites for the mechanism is that the `since` *parameter* exists on the crew tool, and the one change-notification module in the tree (`reckon/change_streams.py`) is an inotify watcher over the docs tree with no retained history, while `reckon/velocity.py` derives plan metas from git history and is not named.
